newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour not committed to Euro in 2000s - Cook.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour not committed to Euro in 2000s - Cook.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party will keep its options open on whether Britain should join a single European currency even in the early years of the next millennium, foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook said on Wednesday.

In a major speech on Britain's relations with Europe, Cook repeated his view, given on television at the weekend, that if the single currency is a success, it would be difficult for Britain to stay outside it.

"It will become increasingly difficult for Britain to go it alone if the single currency succeeds and if over a period of time it proves to have the stability to cope with the strain of differential rates of growth within the single currency areas," Cook said.
But he added: "This emphatically does not mean that Labour is committed to signing up to the single currency in 2001, 2002 or 2003 or any other specific year."
"We are keeping our options for those years every bit as open as our options for 1999."
Cook said Labour would judge the case for British membership of the Euro bloc on Britain's economic interests.
"We will only enter if we are convinced that British industry can compete successfully within a single currency and within the common monetary obligations it will require."
He said while Labour would take the decision on the basis of "a hard-headed assessment of economic reality", a Conservative government's decision would be based on "hysteria and prejudice".
